_README: Clinical knowledge used by step 6. This is NOT produced by the AI. It is a draft summary of widely used diabetic-retinopathy care principles (ICDR severity scale / ophthalmology preferred-practice style guidance). The hospital's ophthalmology lead must review, edit and approve every line against local protocols before any clinical use. No doses are given on purpose.

thresholds._note: dr_high = probability of DR at/above which the eye is flagged HIGH. dr_review = lower, more cautious level that flags MEDIUM. Chosen from validation/test results of the current model; re-check after every re-training.

Retake.label: Image not gradable
Retake.followup: Repeat retinal photography (consider pupil dilation) or arrange a dilated eye examination.
Retake.management: No conclusion about diabetic retinopathy can be drawn from this image.

No DR suspected.label: No diabetic retinopathy suspected by AI
No DR suspected.followup: Routine re-screening, typically every 12 months for a person with diabetes (earlier if symptoms or poor control).
No DR suspected.management: Optimise blood glucose, blood pressure and lipids with the treating physician; lifestyle advice. A normal AI result does not rule out DR.

Possible DR.label: Possible diabetic retinopathy (AI is uncertain)
Possible DR.followup: Clinician review of the image and a dilated eye examination; early re-screen if not examined.
Possible DR.management: Grade to be confirmed by a clinician. Review systemic control (glucose, blood pressure, lipids).
Possible DR.medication: No eye medication should be chosen from an uncertain AI result.

Suspected DR.label: Suspected diabetic retinopathy
Suspected DR.followup: Refer to an ophthalmologist for dilated examination and grading. Timing depends on the confirmed grade (see the grade table).
Suspected DR.management: Grade and presence of macular oedema to be confirmed by a clinician; review systemic control.
Suspected DR.medication: Eye-specific treatment is decided only after grading (see the grade table).

Other finding.label: Possible other retinal finding (e.g. drusen / macular change)
Other finding.management: AI does not identify the specific condition.

No DR.management: Systemic control of glucose, blood pressure and lipids.

Mild NPDR.management: Systemic control of glucose, blood pressure and lipids; patient education on symptoms.

Moderate NPDR.followup: Ophthalmology review; follow-up roughly every 3-6 months (sooner if macular oedema).
Moderate NPDR.management: Intensify systemic control; look for macular oedema.
Moderate NPDR.medication: If centre-involving macular oedema is present: intravitreal anti-VEGF therapy (for example aflibercept, ranibizumab, faricimab; bevacizumab is used where cost is a constraint), or laser, at the specialist's discretion.

Severe NPDR.followup: Prompt referral to a retina specialist (within weeks).
Severe NPDR.management: High risk of progression to proliferative disease; intensify systemic control.
Severe NPDR.medication: Specialist may consider panretinal laser photocoagulation and/or intravitreal anti-VEGF injections.

PDR.medication: Panretinal laser and/or intravitreal anti-VEGF injections; vitrectomy for vitreous haemorrhage or traction (specialist decision).

Diabetic macular oedema.followup: Retina specialist referral; timing by severity and vision.
Diabetic macular oedema.management: Confirm centre involvement with OCT if available.
Diabetic macular oedema.medication: Intravitreal anti-VEGF (aflibercept, ranibizumab, faricimab, or bevacizumab), corticosteroid implants or focal laser per specialist.
